title: Keep the Windows WSL bridge out of Ninja codegen file dependencies
body: The native command cmake --build build/ninja --target recipe_simd_check --parallel 4 failed before running the check: ninja reported C:/Windows/System32/wsl.exe as a missing input for codegen/checks/recipe_simd_check.stamp, even though the WSL bridge was selected at configure. The pinned CodegenTool --recipe-simd-cpp --check invocation passed when run directly through the live queue after regenerating the output. Keep the bridge executable as a command dependency rather than a generated-file input, or publish its resolved path to Ninja as a valid external dependency.

title: Make generated VIXEN headers EOL-stable across Windows and WSL
body: Running the pinned recipe SIMD generator on the Windows checkout made RecipeSimd.g.hpp appear modified in git status while git diff was empty. git ls-files --eol reported i/lf w/mixed, and Git warned CRLF would be replaced by LF. The generator check passed after regeneration, but I had to git restore the exact generated file to normalize it back to w/lf and keep the lane clean. Make the emitter write the repository's canonical LF output on Windows so a fresh check does not leave platform-only worktree drift.

title: Check the Linux Vulkan SDK glslang include path without a false fatal diagnostic
body: A fresh CMake preset vixen-wsl configure with the auto-provisioned LunarG SDK 1.4.350.1 printed the diagnostic Fatal Error: glslang directory not found for <sdk>/x86_64/Include/glslang, although the official Linux SDK has the headers under <sdk>/x86_64/include/glslang. Configure continued and the Dozen target built. Check the Linux case-correct include path and reserve fatal wording for a real configure stop, so a usable SDK does not require manual source inspection.

title: Declare render scale and upscaler stages in the render facade
body: Stage 1 required hand-adding three ComputeStageNodes, three full-frame/intermediate RenderTargetNodes, provider registries, image sync gatherers, target formats, pass dispatches, and topology connections in BuildRenderGraph.cpp. The facade did not declare a reusable upscaler module or derive the render/presentation extent split and hazards. Add a declarative upscaler capability that emits the AA/EASU/RCAS chain, intermediate targets, and synchronization from scale/upscaler configuration.

title: Set up native test runtime DLL paths in the capture launcher
body: The native vixen_lookdev_capture executable failed before test startup with Windows status 0xc0000135 because tbb12.dll was in the build configuration runtime directory but not PATH. I manually added build/stage1-merged-native/msvc_19.44_cxx_64_md_release to PATH and the executable launched. Have the CTest launcher derive and stage or prepend the linked runtime DLL directory.

title: Provide a fixed exposure capture mode for scale comparisons
body: A valid same-look comparison required a frozen exposure, but the production graph always ran per-frame ExposureMeter and ExposureReduce. I added a special fixed exposure shader variant, omitted the meter stage, and selected it through VIXEN_HDR_EXPOSURE_FIXED. Expose fixed EV as a declared capture or authoring mode so experiments do not need a bespoke state guard and shader variant.

title: Make the direct native build route callable from WSL
body: The native build command `cmd.exe /c C:\vixen-native\upscalestage1\.tmp\build-stage1-fsr1-native.bat` failed before starting with exit 127 because cmd.exe was not on WSL PATH. Calling /mnt/c/Windows/System32/cmd.exe with an unquoted Windows batch argument then lost the path backslashes and failed to find the file. The build succeeded with the full cmd.exe path and the batch path passed as a single quoted argument. Provide a documented launcher that preserves WSL interop and Windows path quoting for the direct vcvars64 plus CMake route.

title: Clarify GPU resource locking versus exclusive heavy-slot admission
body: Using the queue for a native look-dev capture, `--resource gpu --exclusive` requested all 15 CPU pair tokens and remained blocked behind active builds. The `gpu` resource alone already acquires the dedicated GPU device lock; without `--exclusive` the same capture ran with two CPU tokens and no overlapping GPU job. Clarify that `--exclusive` reserves both heavy CPU slots, or expose an exclusive GPU-only mode, so an exclusive native GPU witness does not unnecessarily reserve every CPU token.
